question: The graph of \(y=kx\) passes through point \((2,6)\). What is the value of \(k\)?
solution: Substitute \(x=2\) and \(y=6\) into \(y=kx\) to obtain \(6=2k\), so \(k=3\).

nodes.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.
nodes.label: 7.RP.A.2b

nodes.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.
nodes.label: 7.RP.A.2

nodes.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.
nodes.label: 7.RP.A.2a

nodes.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole- number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane. Use tables to compare ratios.
nodes.label: 6.RP.A.3a

nodes.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations. For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.
nodes.label: 7.RP.A.2c

nodes.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways. For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.
nodes.label: 8.EE.B.5

nodes.description: Use variables to represent two quantities in a real-world problem that change in relationship to one another; write an equation to express one quantity, thought of as the dependent variable, in terms of the other quantity, thought of as the independent variable. Analyze the relationship between the dependent and independent variables using graphs and tables, and relate these to the equation. For example, in a problem involving motion at constant speed, list and graph ordered pairs of distances and times, and write the equation d = 65t to represent the relationship between distance and time.
nodes.label: 6.EE.C.9

nodes.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.
nodes.label: 7.RP.A.2d

Perpendicular constructions and uniqueness explain orthogonal projections, but plotting on an existing square grid needs only its given axes. Keep the useful geometry preparation without imposing the full construction workflow.
Each coordinate axis is a number line with an origin, a direction and a unit. Plotting and reading coordinates is impossible without understanding those three elements of a number line.
edges.scope: coordinate axes as two perpendicular number lines

edges.reason: Each axis is a signed number line, so plotting signed coordinates uses number-to-position interpretation on it.
edges.scope: axes as number lines with negatives

edges.reason: A point's two coordinates form an ordered pair; swapping the entries generally changes the point.
Connecting tables, formulas and graphs prepares proportional-function work, but the comparative representation repertoire is not required to recognize y=kx and plot its points.

Earlier positive-quantity constant-ratio experience motivates y=kx. The signed-real function definition and coordinate graph can be introduced directly, so the earlier lesson is preparation rather than a distinct necessary input.

Decimal addition/subtraction helps solve and check equations with decimal constants. The source places no integer-only restriction, so Gemini's integer example disproves necessity without disproving this useful preparation; integer equations avoid the decimal algorithm.
edges.scope: equations with decimal coefficients or constants
